### Observed differences

- In the later window, A27, A36, A37, A42 and A43 appear in every trace (up from roughly 47–54 in 100 cases), A02 participates about three times as often (about 28 in 100 vs 8), and A10 nearly disappears (about 3 in 100 vs 11.5). [OCC001, OCC002, OCC003, OCC004, OCC005, OCC006, OCC007]
- The order between A26/A28 and the A36–A43 group reverses: earlier, A26 and A28 each preceded A36/A37/A42/A43 in about 53 in 100 traces and essentially never followed them; in the later window the group precedes A26 and A28 in about 99 in 100. A27, which almost never co-occurred with the group before (under 1 in 100), now co-occurs in every trace with the group before it; A28 now always precedes A27 (about 47 in 100 before), and A27 now precedes A31 in about 99.5 in 100 (about 47 before). [REL026, REL027, REL028, REL029, REL030, REL031, REL032, REL033, REL034, REL035, REL036, REL037, REL038, REL039]
- A14, A25 and A15 now co-occur with A27 and the A36–A43 group in every trace (previously about 47–54 in 100, with many traces containing one but not the other), and A14/A25 precede the group in about 99 in 100. [REL010, REL011, REL012, REL013, REL014, REL015, REL020, REL021, REL022, REL023, REL024, REL025]
- Routing changed accordingly: A25's outgoing transitions shift from almost exclusively A28 (about 98.5 in 100) to A43, A37, A42 and A36 (roughly 18–28 in 100 each), and the immediate A25→A28 step (lag 1 in about 99 in 100 cases) becomes a gap of about five steps; A26's outgoing transitions concentrate on A27 (about 98.5 in 100, from about 45); the group's transitions now go to A28 (about 24–28 in 100) where they previously went to A31 (about 19–29 in 100, now unobserved). [DIR003, DIR004, DIR005, DIR006, DIR007, DIR008, LAG004]
- Positions move consistently with this: A36/A37/A42/A43 occur earlier (mean relative position about 0.58 to about 0.40 of the trace), while A26 and A28 occur later (about 0.53 to 0.61 and 0.39 to 0.47). [POS004, POS006, POS008, POS009, POS010, POS011]
- A02 occurs much earlier (mean relative position about 0.51 to 0.19), typically right after A14, routes mainly to A15 (about 86 in 100 of its observed outgoing transitions, vs about 18 before), and precedes A25/A26/A27 and the A36–A43 group in about 25 in 100 traces (about 2–4 before). [OCC001, POS001, DIR001, DIR002, LAG001, LAG002, REL001, REL003, REL006]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports the possibility that the flow was restructured so that the A36/A37/A42/A43 group became an unconditional step, performed in every case and placed between the A14/A25 segment and the A26/A28/A27/A31 tail: A25, which previously passed almost directly to A28, now feeds into the group, and A26 now leads almost exclusively to A27, which the group now precedes and A31 follows. A02 additionally behaves as a more frequent, early activity inserted after A14 and leading mainly to A15. [REL026, REL030, REL031, REL032, REL025, DIR003, DIR004, OCC003, OCC004, OCC001, POS001, DIR001]

The hypothesis rests on directly observed relational and positional change rather than participation alone: order reversals and co-occurrence shares, successor-profile changes, a step-distance change and position shifts all point the same way, and the defining after-window relations (the group before A26/A28, the group co-occurring with A27) were essentially absent earlier, so they are not explained by frequency shifts of already-known variants. The volume of qualifying items (82) is also roughly 80 times the about 1 expected if nothing had changed. [REL026, REL032, REL036, DIR003, DIR004, LAG004, POS008, OCC003]

Limitations: several items re-describe one underlying trace change (for example the four order flips between A26 and A36/A37/A42/A43), so they are not independent confirmations; positions and lags use event positions, not clock time; and the A02 pattern rests on fewer traces (about 16 before vs 55 after) with very thin before-window support in the lag data. A competing explanation that cannot be fully ruled out is a shift in the mix of pre-existing trace variants — a rare after-window variant displacing the common before-window ones — although the near-complete absence of the new orderings in the earlier window makes pure sampling fluctuation an unlikely account. [REL026, REL027, REL028, REL029, OCC001, LAG001, LAG002]

Let me analyse this evidence carefully.

Setup:
- 200 traces before, 200 traces after.
- Screening: 198 units tested, 0.99 items expected without change.
- Evidence items: let me count. OCC001-OCC007 (7), DIR001-DIR009 (9), POS001-POS011 (11), REL001-REL049 (49), LAG001-LAG006 (6). Total = 7+9+11+49+6 = 82 items.

82 items vs 0.99 expected without change — that's many times larger, so chance as a whole cannot explain the count. So we move past the "insufficient evidence by count" gate.

Now judge by directness, consistency, and ability to rule out competing explanations.

Key behavioural patterns:

1. A02: participation rose from 8% to 27.5% of traces (OCC001), mean occurrences 0.09 → 0.29. Position moved earlier: mean position 0.51 → 0.19 (POS001). Direction profile changed drastically: before, outgoing transitions spread across many targets (A16 ~18%, A20 ~12%, A30 ~12%, A19 ~12%, A52 ~12%...), after, A15 dominates at ~86% (DIR001). Support: 17 → 57 outgoing transitions observed.

2. A10: participation dropped from 11.5% to 3% (OCC002).

3. A27: participation rose from 46.5% to 100% (OCC003), mean occurrences 0.465 → 1.0. Position slightly later: mean 0.594 → 0.640 (POS005).

4. A36, A37, A42, A43: participation rose from ~54% to 100% (OCC004-007), and positions moved earlier: A36 mean 0.58 → 0.41 (POS008), A37 0.58 → 0.40 (POS009), A42 0.59 → 0.41 (POS010), A43 0.57 → 0.40 (POS011).

5. A25: position slightly earlier (POS003, mean 0.36 → 0.336). DIR003: A25's outgoing transitions changed completely — before ~98.5% to A28, after spread across A43 (~28%), A42 (~25%), A37 (~27%), A36 (~18%). That's a big routing change.

6. A26: DIR004 — before, outgoing spread across A27 (~45%), A43 (~16%), A36 (~13%), A42 (~11%), A37 (~11%); after, ~98.5% to A27. POS004: A26 position moved later, mean 0.53 → 0.61.

7. A28: POS006 — position moved later, mean 0.39 → 0.47.

8. REL items: massive changes.
   - A02 with A25/A26/A28/A31: cooccurrence rose from ~8% to 27.5%, A_before_B rose from ~2.5-4% to ~25% (REL001-REL005). So A02 now occurs before these activities in about 25 in 100 traces.

   - A26 with A36/A37/A42/A43: order flipped! Before, A26 before A36 etc. in ~53%; after, A36 before A26 in ~99% (REL026-REL029). This is a complete order reversal.
   - A27 with A36/A37/A42/A43: before, they were mostly mutually exclusive (A_only ~46%, B_only ~53%, cooccurrence ~0); after, cooccurrence 100% with A27... wait, B_before_A ~99% means A36 before A27? Let me check REL032: values [A27, A36]. A_before_B 0.0, B_before_A 0.99. So A36 before A27 in 99% of traces after. Before, A_only 0.46 (A27 without A36), B_only 0.535 (A36 without A27), cooccurrence 0.005.
   - A28 with A36/A37/A42/A43: before A28 before A36 ~52.5%; after A36 before A28 ~99% (REL036-REL039). Order reversal.
   - A31 with A36/A37/A42/A43: before A31 before A36 ~52% (B_before_A since A=A31, B=A36: B_before_A 0.52); after B_before_A 0.985 (REL040-REL043). Consistent direction, strengthened.

   - LAG001 (A02→A15): before only 1 observation, after 51; lag-1 share rose to ~51%. Weak before-support.
